absent: Numeric encodings of shadow masks, writability and size bits, non-present marker, reverse-map flags, paging levels, and performance control reserved values.
Ordering among virtual machine memory lock, translation page lock, reference counting, and RCU reclamation across concurrent paths.
Translation lookaside invalidation, fast fault handling, and aging interactions that surround entry clearing and promotion.
Vendor-specific performance model realization behind the static dispatch and host event configuration details.
Guest frame to slot resolution, slot lifetime, and per-level array sizing beyond offset indexing.
Slab cache initialization and deferred destruction timing for descriptor blocks and shadow pages.
Guest-visible fault behavior for reserved control bits and for MMIO versus present entries.

findings.text: Releases one reference on a translation root and retires it only on final release, detaching it from global tracking and deferring reclamation until readers drain. Final release is valid solely for invalid translation pages.

Rebuilds the virtual performance monitoring model for a virtual processor after discarding prior counter state, establishing neutral limits before delegating to vendor logic and then publishing usable counter availability.
Reports whether clearing a shadow entry must use atomic handling because of concurrent promotion, access tracking, or hardware status updates.

Each shadow entry address resolves to its owning page through host address translation plus frame metadata, and masked entry values resolve to child pages. Special zero-frame roots denote absence rather than a page, and legacy segment roots are normalized through the same child resolution. The position of an entry inside its page derives from pointer alignment.

Entry properties that steer update and caching decisions are determined from flag combinations covering software writability intent, hardware writability, access and dirty tracking enablement, large mapping indication, terminal level status, and masked MMIO identity combined with a global caching allowance.

Cleared entries always land in a defined non-present state regardless of update path, and per-level residency accounting is adjusted only when the displaced value had been present. Removal from reverse tracking happens only in that present case.
Reverse tracking for an entry is found through role-selected slot sets plus frame-offset indexing into per-level arrays, using the owning page and intra-page position to recover the guest frame.

Reverse-map mutation and observation require write hold on the virtual machine memory lock, with low-level acquisition additionally requiring disabled preemption. Acquisition spins on a transient flag and uses acquire semantics paired with release on unlock. Global translation root tracking uses separate spin serialization for list detachment.

A reverse head is empty, a single direct entry pointer, or a flagged chain of descriptor blocks, plus a transient locked indication that is stripped for readers and never persisted as the new stable value.

Multi-entry tracking keeps tail blocks full while the head block absorbs size changes. Removal replaces the vacated slot with the last head slot and frees the head block when it empties, collapsing to empty or to the next block as head.

Parent linkage for a shadow page is tracked as a reverse set that supports draining one entry at a time. Dropping a parent removes its reverse entry and returns the link to non-present without residency accounting.

Stale subtree handling moves between clean, marked with a count plus per-slot marks, collected into a bounded vector, and reclaimed with ancestor marks cleared upward until a marked ancestor remains. Stale marks for absent or large links are pruned without collection, duplicate unsynchronized pages are coalesced, and leaf pages have no children to collect.

Entry clearing selects between a fast store and an atomic exchange based on presence and concurrent mutation risk, with the exchange variant ensuring ordered visibility of the replacement. Both variants converge on the same non-present result and conditional accounting.

The virtual performance model cycles through gated entry, quiescing of active host bindings with zeroing of emulated state, publication of neutral limits, vendor realization unless globally disabled, and finally default enablement plus availability publication for general and fixed counters.

Observed counter values combine retained emulated progress with live host progress when bound and unpaused, masked to the counter width. Mediated mode observes only retained progress masked to width, and stopping preserves the observed value before releasing the host binding.

Model changes are allowed only before first guest entry and outside nested execution. Global control emulation requires a model version above one, and mediated operation additionally requires a global allowance plus a nonzero version.
Cached fault address state is cleared when the caller uses a wildcard or when the cached page matches the supplied address page, otherwise it is retained.

The reserved control register set starts from an architectural base and additionally reserves each optional feature control whose host capability is absent, with one combined control reserved only when both constituent features are absent.
Virtual processor requests are recorded only for actions the target must handle, enforced at build time for constant request identifiers that must not carry a no-action marker.

Non-atomic replacement risks losing concurrent writable promotion, access-track restoration, or hardware status updates. Tolerance for access-bit imprecision does not extend to writable state lacking dirty indication, which still demands atomic handling, as does any entry with disabled access and dirty tracking.

Unexpected reverse-map contents, missing list membership, or empty head removal attempts are treated as data corruption that either traps or taints the virtual machine once, rather than proceeding silently.

Four-kilobyte level denotes terminal paging depth for last-entry and child-collection decisions, intra-page position derives from fixed entry density, guest frame lookup is indexed per level, and reverse heads distinguish single, chained, empty, and locked encodings.
Reclamation enters through draining of a page parent set and through bounded collection plus invalidation of stale descendants of a non-leaf parent.
Operational entries exist for recording a virtual processor request and for conditionally invalidating cached fault address state.
Translation roots remain globally tracked while referenced, with final release validating translation type and invalid marking before detach and deferred destruction.
Legacy segment root validity is equivalent to a nonzero handle value.
